Contour Maps

Published

October 31, 2025

Modified

May 29, 2026

Abstract
Contour and Relief Maps using the tanaka package

1 Introduction

2 Goals

At the end of this Lab session, we should:

  • Understand the concept of a contour map
  • Useraster form data to construct contour maps with them
  • Use the tanaka package and appreciate the Tanaka Method
  • And of course, add our own data to the contour maps made with tanaka

3 Setting up R Packages

# Plotting Maps
library(tidyverse) # Maps using ggplot() + geom_sf()
library(ggformula) # Maps using gf_sf()
# For Spatial Data Frame Processing
library(sf)
library(sfheaders) # Handcrafted Map data
# library(terra)
library(tidyterra) # tidy syntax for terra operations + plotting
library(stars)
## Plotting
library(tanaka)
# Spatial Data
library(geodata)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
# Run this in your console first
# devtools::install_github("ropensci/rnaturalearthhires")
library(rnaturalearthhires)
library(elevatr) # Get Elevation data

4 Contour Maps

Let us plot a basic contour map, with the tanaka package.

ras <- get_elev_raster(locations = data.frame(x = c(6.7, 7), y = c(45.8, 46)), z = 10,
    prj = "+init=epsg:4326", clip = "locations") %>%
    as.raster()
plot(ras)
# create the isopleth layer
iso <- tanaka_contour(x = ras, breaks = seq(500, 4800, 250))
Error:
! 'x' should be a data.frame, an sf data.frame a SpatVector or a SpatRaster.
# display the isopleth layer
plot(st_geometry(iso))
Error in `h()`:
! error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'plot': object 'iso' not found
